title: resilience-fuzz-suite-for-partial-streams-and-schema-relaxation-tests
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a focused test harness that simulates partial/garbled streaming output, constrained-decoder backoff behavior, and schema-relaxation fallbacks across model variants and quantization profiles. Goal is to catch regressions where streaming + function/tool calling or token-level truncation leads to invalid JSON payloads or silent schema drift. The suite will be integrated into CI and run nightly against a matrix of runtime kernels and model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly CI job executes the fuzz-suite against at least 3 model variants (float32, q4_0, q6_k) and reports pass/fail via GH status
At least 25 deterministic fuzz vectors cover token-drop, mid-token split, escaped-quote corruption, and toolcall-interleaving during streaming

Constrained-decoder backoff behaviour is exercised: when token-level decoding fails, runtime must attempt configured fallbacks (relax-schema, switch-to-plain-text) and emit an explicit diagnostics envelope
Regression dashboard created with per-test flaky-rate and historical failure trends (link in ticket)
Documentation and runbook for oncall describing triage steps for schema violations from streaming inputs
test_plan: Corpus generation: create deterministic and randomized prompt+schema pairs (1000 deterministic, 10k fuzzed variants)
Network simulation: introduce token loss, reordering, duplication at the streaming transport layer to emulate edge cases
Function/tool call interference: simulate tool responses injected mid-stream and validate tool-return schema enforcement vs. main schema
Constrained-decoder checks: validate enforcement thresholds (strict, moderate, lenient) and ensure decoder falls back per-config
Compatibility checks: run tests with legacy "loose-json" clients to verify graceful degradation and explicit compatibility headers
Golden fixtures: maintain a set of 50 golden prompts that must remain stable across runtime changes
implementation_notes: Add new test harness module runtime/tests/stream_fuzz that can drive sockets and apply byte-level faults
Leverage existing CI matrix infra and add nightly job: ci/nightly/streaming-schema-fuzz.yaml
Expose failure artifacts (raw token stream, reconstructed JSON, diff to schema) to S3 for triage
Mark highly flaky cases with metadata to reduce alert noise and create follow-up tasks to harden runtime paths
Provide lightweight local runner (python) for engineers to reproduce failing vectors quickly
Coordinate with QA to add an exploratory session specifically focused on function call reentrancy
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff — scoped corpus generators and identified 4 primary fault categories (drop, split, duplicate, corruption)
2025-02-14: Prototype harness that injects byte-level faults into streaming socket; validated against small LLM container locally
2025-02-17: Added deterministic golden fixtures and initial 200 fuzz vectors; discovered a decoder bug where mid-stream toolcall tokens were appended to main JSON object
2025-02-20: Implemented artifact upload (S3) and dashboard skeleton; created GH draft PR for harness (see reviews)
Next: expand matrix to include q8_0 experiments and schedule 48-hour flaky triage window
reviews: PR feedback from @sarah.kim: prefer using existing socket-mock library to reduce maintenance; adjust fixture naming to be versioned
Feedback from @omar.patel: ensure fallback diagnostic envelope contains request-id and model-variant to speed triage
Security note from @maria.li: S3 artifacts must be encrypted and access-limited; update bucket policy before enabling public CI run
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Nightly runs may produce high noise due to inherent fuzz nondeterminism. Mitigation: seed randomness, record seeds, and mark flaky vectors for separate handling.
Risk: Large artifact volume. Mitigation: sample artifacts retained and rotate older data after 30d; compress raw streams.
Risk: Pulling model variants into CI increases infra cost. Mitigation: run heavier quantized variants less frequently and use synthetic microbenchmarks for quick feedback.
next_steps: Merge GH draft PR for harness and iterate based on CI failures
Expand fuzz corpus to 5k deterministic vectors and add q8_0 run
Coordinate with runtime release owners to run the suite before runtime-1.19 cut
